summary: 中考 reading round 2: final check of the corrected passages (+canaries) in groups, 2 finders + 2 verifiers per group

findings.current: the future of sustainable construction could progress
findings.reason: Illogical comparison. The sentence says 'the future' could progress faster 'than in the past', but the future has no progress in the past to compare with. What progresses is sustainable construction. Deleting 'the future of' gives the intended meaning. Treat this as a judgment call: it is the least certain finding in this report.

va.why: This is not a definite error. 'The future of X' is a common journalistic way of saying 'the development of X' (compare 'the future of work is changing faster than ever'). The same idiom appears in ¶2 ('may lie with AI') and in ¶4 ('speed up the future of sustainable construction'), and both are being kept. The exam paper reads the same way. This is a style preference, and the proposer called it the least certain finding.

vb.why: Using 'the future of X' to mean how X develops is a standard journalistic metonymy, and the same pattern appears in ¶4 ('speed up the future of sustainable construction'). The sentence matches the exam and apparently the original Inhabitat article, and the comparison is easy to understand. The proposer calls this a judgment call, and it is a style tightening rather than a definite error.

findings.current: which are this year’s theme flower
findings.proposed: which is this year’s theme flower
findings.reason: Subject-verb agreement. 'the iris' is singular (and 'theme flower' is singular), so the verb must be 'is'. The exam paper itself reads 'which is', so this is an unlisted change that introduced an error.
Pronoun agreement. The antecedent is 'the Nanshan garden', which is singular, so the pronoun must be 'it'. The exam paper reads 'calling it'.

findings.current: Gardens are small, so they carry
findings.proposed: Gardens are small, but they carry
findings.reason: Wrong connective. Carrying big ideas is a contrast with being small, not a result of it, so 'so' makes the sentence illogical. The exam paper reads 'but'.
April has only 30 days, so 'April 31' cannot be a date. The exam paper says the show 'ran through April 6'.
Subject–verb agreement: the antecedent "the iris" is singular and so is the complement "this year’s theme flower". The exam paper itself reads "which is".
Wrong pronoun reference: the antecedent "the Nanshan garden" is singular. The exam paper reads "calling it".

va.why: The current text matches exactly. 'the iris ... which are this year's theme flower' is wrong because the antecedent and the complement are both singular, so the verb must be 'is'. The exam dump (line 32) reads 'which is'. Same fix as index 5, so apply it only once.

The current text matches exactly. 'the Nanshan garden, calling them shiny and bright' is wrong because the antecedent is one garden, so the pronoun must be 'it'. The exam dump reads 'calling it'. Same fix as index 6, so apply it only once.

The current text matches exactly. 'Gardens are small, so they carry big ideas' is illogical, because carrying big ideas contrasts with being small; it does not follow from it. 'but' is the correct, minimal fix, and the exam dump (line 34) reads 'but'.
'April 31' cannot be a date because April has only 30 days. The exam dump (line 35) reads 'ran through April 6', so 'April 6' is the correct, minimal fix.
Same as index 0. 'which are this' matches the text, the antecedent 'the iris' is singular, and the exam reads 'which is'. Apply the fix only once.
Same as index 1. 'calling them shiny' matches the text, the antecedent 'the Nanshan garden' is singular, and the exam reads 'calling it'. Apply the fix only once.

vb.why: 'the iris ... which are this year's theme flower' breaks subject-verb agreement, since both the antecedent and the complement are singular. The exam dump reads 'which is', so the file has picked up an error the paper does not have.
The antecedent 'the Nanshan garden' is singular, so the pronoun must be 'it'. The exam dump reads 'calling it shiny and bright'.
'small, so they carry big ideas' is illogical because carrying big ideas contrasts with being small; it does not follow from it. The exam dump reads 'but'.
April 31 does not exist. The exam dump reads 'ran through April 6'.
This duplicates index 0. It is a real agreement error, and the exam dump confirms 'which is'.
This duplicates index 1. The pronoun for the singular 'the Nanshan garden' must be 'it', and the exam dump confirms 'calling it'.
